Simon / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

What we heard:
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency on your in-house recommender during peak traffic burst windows (target 95p < 120ms).
- Current infra: mixed CPU/GPU with ~2.5s cold-starts for large models; looking for predictable tail latency and lower cost per 1M tokens.
- Success criteria: measurable latency improvement in a 2-week POC + cost delta report.

Proposed POC (high level):
1) 2-week private deployment (VPC) using a quantized model variant and Redwood caching to validate 95p latency and cost numbers.
2) Baseline run + 3-day load window + final report.

Attachments: Calyx-POC-outline.pdf (proposal), redwood-pricing-quote-20270205.xlsx (ballpark).

Immediate next steps:
- You: confirm priority and internal sponsor for the POC (engineering & infra).
- Us: prepare a technical runbook and sample traffic guide (Dev will draft).
- If greenlit, we’ll schedule a 30–45m kickoff with SE + infra within 3–5 business days.

I’ll follow up early next week if I don’t hear back. Thanks — looking forward to it.

—

Simon/Priya — quick answers below:
- Recommended infra: 1–2 x A10G-class GPUs for warm inference + 1 smaller T4 node for background batch jobs. If you’re constrained, a single A10G with autoscale is fine for the 2-week POC.
- Cache: enable prefix/KV cache for session-affine requests. For recommender use, an in-memory KV cache (co-located) will reduce cold-start latency and avoid repeating expensive token work.
- Statefulness: not required for the POC — we’ll emulate sessions; if long-term, we can evaluate sticky routes.

I’ll draft a 1-page runbook (instance sizes, expected throughput, token budget) and post it to the Drive link Logan shared.

—Dev
